This PR fixes a crash on RISC-V CPUs without Zba when Shenandoah's C2 load-reference-barrier slow path is taken. `ShenandoahBarrierStubC2::lrb()` zero-extends the narrowOop returned by the LRB runtime call with `MacroAssembler::zext_w()`, which is a Zba pseudo instruction that leaves the `UseZba` check to its caller. pulls.author: albertnetymk
pulls.body_excerpt: This change makes the Parallel GC generation boundary dynamic. The heap is still reserved as one contiguous range, with old gen at lower addresses and young gen at higher addresses, but the boundary between them can now move during GC. The current implementation fixes the old/young reserved split at startup. This limits how much reserved space each generation can use later.
